name: Compass Pointe
award: 2024 Federal 4% and state housing tax credits (Round Two)
headline: Kittle Property Group is building Compass Pointe, 192 income-restricted one- to four-bedroom apartments in six buildings for households at 30% to 80% AMI on a 14-acre site at Oakshire Lane and Beaumont Street in Pueblo's Eastwood neighborhood; it won 2024 Round Two federal 4% and accelerated state credits with $38.5M of CHFA bonds after two earlier tries.
why_it_matters: It is one of the largest family LIHTC deals in Pueblo in years and shows a vertically integrated national sponsor filling a non-metro gap with city HOME money, assigned city bond cap, a $2M Division of Housing loan and a housing authority tax-exemption partnership.

status.label: Financing closed and construction under way (inferred); completion targeted 2027
status.detail: Kittle's November 2025 announcement describes the project as financed by CHFA bonds, US Bank construction loan and equity, Cedar Rapids Bank & Trust permanent loan, and city HOME and DOH loans (closing inferred), and the Pueblo Housing Authority calls its special limited partner role a 2025 milestone. On 2026-10-20 the City of Pueblo said the project is scheduled for completion in 2027, and the county assessor lists a clubhouse with year built 2026. No building permit numbers were found.

next_step: Watch Pueblo Regional Building Department records for certificates of occupancy and the start of lease-up in 2027.

key_numbers.meaning: 48 one-bedroom, 72 two-bedroom, 64 three-bedroom and 8 four-bedroom units, using income averaging from 30% to 80% AMI (133 units at 60%).
About $36.2M over 10 years, plus $1,800,000 of accelerated state credit.
CHFA is the issuer, with City of Pueblo bond cap assigned to the deal; the application expected about $22.3M of long-term bonds and a roughly $16.5M taxable tail during construction.
A $750,000 City of Pueblo HOME loan and a $2 million Colorado Division of Housing loan, per the sponsor.

facts.value: Southwest corner of Oakshire Lane and Beaumont Street, Pueblo 81001; assessor situs 2620-2680 Oakshire Ln, Lot 1 Compass Pointe Subdivision (parcel 04-282-51-002, 14.176 acres)
Six residential buildings (four three-story, two two-story), a freestanding clubhouse, a maintenance building and five garage buildings with 36 garages
Clubhouse with leasing office, pool, fitness center, business center, game room, dog park, in-unit washers and dryers
All-electric; residents pay sub-metered utilities except trash; NGBS certification
Eastwood neighborhood, in a Qualified Census Tract; next to a Veterans Affairs facility, a solar garden and a park; transit stop within 225 feet; Baca Elementary about 425 feet away
Zoned correctly for the use, per the application
Housing Authority of the City of Pueblo is the special limited partner; the application planned property and sales/use tax exemption through it. The assessor shows an exempt value starting in 2026
Resident services from local providers, United Way and YWCA Pueblo

background.text: Compass Pointe LP bought the vacant 14.2-acre site on 2025-06-23 for $550,000 by special warranty deed (reception 2377424) from members of the Concialdi and Colalancia families, who had owned it since 1993.

The 2024 award was the project's third CHFA application. The 2022 Round Two version was 132 units (32 one-, 68 two-, 24 three- and 8 four-bedroom) at 30%, 50% and 60% AMI; the 2023 Round Two version added 60 units to reach the current 192-unit, six-building plan with the same income mix.
The application cites an 8.3% capture rate, 0% vacancy in the market area, a Pueblo Housing Authority waitlist of 2,007 applicants, and lease-up of 15 units a month with no concessions.

The Pueblo Housing Authority's director described the partnership as a way to move households who have improved their incomes out of subsidized units and free those units for families most in need, per the application.
Letters of support came from the Mayor, the Pueblo Housing Authority, the Chamber of Commerce and the YWCA, per the application. The Phase I found no recognized environmental conditions.
No project-based vouchers or homeless set-aside are described.
